Progress declared via optimistic self-assertion ('95% complete', 'all 44+ routes work', 'feeds work') and a feature inventory; never verified against the reference. No differential harness exists, so status is implementation-presence, not parity pass/fail.

Caught self-inflicted regressions when its own sed/python edits broke the build (51 errors; corrupted string literal) and reverted — regression awareness at compile level only, not parity-level regression of a previously-passing subsystem.

Looped on the multipart content_disposition fix and repeatedly corrupted main.rs using the same sed/python-edit tactic without recognizing the thrash or switching approach — the opposite of catching circular re-debugging early.
Repeated TodoWrite reminders ignored; no structured ledger and, critically, no side-by-side reference comparison ever run, so 'passing/failing/not-attempted' was never distinguished on evidence.

reasoning: The agent sustained a running prose checklist of subsystem status and updated it as features landed (matching the structure of anchor 5), and it caught some self-inflicted build regressions and reverted. But the 'status' was unverified implementation-presence rather than harness-backed parity, done-claims were optimistic assertions on build-success/inventory, and it failed to recognize repeated file-corruption thrash — falling short of anchor 5's true parity tracking and well below the harness-backed, regression-aware, thrash-detecting behavior of anchor 8. This places it at 4, between vague recollection (3) and a genuine parity checklist (5).
